spec_match.rationale: Exercises the exact three-method session lifecycle (startDiagnosticLogging resolves a UUID, finishDiagnosticLogging finalises, cancelDiagnosticLogging discards) and resolves whichever binding the browser ships — Chrome 151's navigator.rtc (Chromium navigator_rtc.idl/rtc.idl, verified 2026-08-16) or the current WICG draft's RTCPeerConnection statics — with the active shape reported to the visitor; the spec's silent-resolve note is stated and linked to the concept that demonstrates it.

interactive.rationale: Real state-gated buttons make the real calls and drive the state machine, session-ID readout, and timestamped call log; when neither binding exists the controls are honestly disabled with the exact enable steps (flag, experimental-features flag, OT registration link) — never a faked session.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card promises the three-call state machine with a live session ID and per-state button gating; the page delivers exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the unbound-browser branch (disabled controls + exact prerequisites), per-call rejection paths rendered into the log and status line, and documents the spec's second-start silent-resolve semantics with a pointer to the loopback concept that observes it.

references.rationale: See-also cites chromestatus.com/feature/5091582546149376 directly; the flag note links the origin-trial registration; the feature index carries spec, explainer, initial proposal, rtc.cc, and policy links.

conformance.rationale: New v151 feature suite (8 assertions) covers the spec-draft statics, the Chrome 151 navigator.rtc binding, the [SecureContext] gate, and metadata-limit rejection on both start and finish, accepting TypeError (spec) or RangeError (Chromium main) so it asserts enforcement, not a transitory error name; executed live at /v151/webrtc-diagnostic-logging-api/conformance/ (1 pass / 7 fail in the unbound harness browser, honest).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP (the sanctioned cloud fallback; chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment): page loads clean, buttons correctly disabled, binding line and flag note render, zero console errors, screenshots read at desktop and 360px mobile. PARTIAL because the harness browser predates the API entirely (RTCDiagnosticLogging does not exist in Chromium 141 even behind flags — verified by probing with --enable-blink-features=RTCDiagnosticLogging), so the bound success path (real UUID, finish/cancel resolution) was not runtime-verified.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts per branch: rtc-start-returns-id / rtc-start failure / rtc-finish / rtc-cancel, plus the explicit rtc-lifecycle-unavailable-fallback assert observed firing in the unbound harness; no failed same-origin requests during validation (telemetry admin endpoint not checked — no credentials in this environment).

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only (including --accent-amber defined in public/styles.css), state boxes invert background+color together, shared classes for shell, code tokens wrap via overflow-wrap:anywhere.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons with visible method-name labels, role=status + aria-live on the status line, role=log on the call log, aria-live on session ID and binding line, decorative state diagram aria-hidden with the same state mirrored in text; keyboard-only operation uses the native button order.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: deno task responsive-check v151/webrtc-diagnostic-logging-api: desktop OK, mobile OK; this concept additionally measured 0px horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3 with zero console errors, and the 360px screenshot was read: state boxes wrap to a column, buttons full-width tappable, log legible.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the bound success path on Chrome 151+ with the RTCDiagnosticLogging flag
openQuestions.detail: The verification environment ships Chromium 141, which predates the API entirely, so only the honest unbound branch could be runtime-verified. In a session with Chrome 151+ (or Canary), relaunch with --enable-blink-features=RTCDiagnosticLogging and drive start → finish and start → cancel, confirming the UUID readout, state transitions, and telemetry asserts on the success path.

guidanceConsulted.query: status live region announcements for async API call results
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer native elements; announce dynamic state through live regions; give every control an accessible name; be deliberate about disabled semantics.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: role=status/aria-live on the status line, role=log for the call log, aria-live on the session-ID and binding readouts, native buttons named by the exact method they call; native disabled is used because the state machine legitimately removes invalid actions and the reason is stated in an adjacent visible note.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP-driven runs 2026-08-16: live-region content observed updating; zero console errors

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table no horizontal overflow narrow mobile viewport
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use flexible wrapping layouts and intrinsic sizing so long tokens and control rows adapt to narrow viewports without horizontal overflow.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: flex-wrap on the state machine and control rows, overflow-wrap:anywhere on code tokens; measured 0px overflow at 360×740.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: mobile-check CDP run 2026-08-16: scrollWidth − innerWidth = 0 at 360px

summary: v151 adaptation of the v150 lifecycle demo for the refiled milestone: all milestone references updated (crumbs /v151/, Chrome 151, OT window 151–156 with the now-public registration link), plus two substantive upgrades found by re-research — dual binding resolution (Chrome 151's navigator.rtc vs the WICG draft's new RTCPeerConnection statics, with the active shape reported) and the spec's silent-resolve second-start note. Verified with headless Chromium 141 CDP (fallback branch only; bound path is an open question) and the responsive matrix.
